answer: Semantic Similarity Slashing: validators must defend proposals in their own words, and pairwise embedding distance below a threshold flags clones. The lantern illuminates copied rationales, since paraphrase detection sits at each graph vertex of submissions. Mutual slashing then burns both stake and reputation when two accounts share a terrace of identical phrasing. A farm running 50 sockpuppets needs 50 genuinely distinct arguments, so cost scales linearly with identities while rewards stay flat — the attacker's margin dies before ten accounts. It works because faking diversity costs more.
